classification.difficultyReason: Reverse the chosen seeds and repeatedly apply the same rule, preserving order and the supplied example.

content.prompt: Swap your two seed numbers from Activity 2 around and figure out the first 20 terms in the new Fibonacci sequence. (If, for example, your sequence in Activity 2 started 6, 11, 17, 28, 45, …, your new sequence will start 11, 6, 17, 23, 40, …) Yes, you do get quite different numbers from the ones in Activity 2.

answer.worked:
Reverse the actual two seeds you chose in Activity 2 and apply the same addition rule. For the sample seeds $11,6$, this produces:

$11, 6, 17, 23, 40, 63, 103, 166, 269, 435$.

$704, 1139, 1843, 2982, 4825, 7807, 12632, 20439, 33071, 53510$. The third term is the same because $6+11=11+6$, but later terms depend on the seed order.
